questions.question: What is heat in physics?
choices: A substance stored inside hot objects
Energy transferred because of a temperature difference
The mass of vibrating particles
The number of particles in an object

questions.question: What does temperature describe in a basic particle model?
choices: The total energy of every particle combined
The object's mass only
A quantity related to average particle kinetic energy
The energy created by every collision

questions.question: What is conduction?
choices: Energy transfer only by moving whole fluids
Energy transfer only by electromagnetic waves
Transfer that requires a vacuum
Energy transfer through interactions within or between contacting materials

questions.question: What is convection?
choices: Energy transfer only through solid metal
Energy transfer only by visible light
Energy transfer associated with bulk movement of a fluid
Energy transfer without any fluid motion

questions.question: What is thermal radiation?
choices: Energy transfer by electromagnetic waves
Movement of hot fluid only
Transfer requiring direct physical contact
The expansion of every solid

questions.question: What is specific heat capacity?
choices: The total mass of a hot sample
Energy needed per unit mass for a unit temperature increase
The temperature at which every substance melts
The rate of radioactive decay

questions.question: What is thermal equilibrium between objects?
choices: A condition of equal mass
A condition in which particles stop moving
A condition of equal temperature with no net heat transfer between them
A condition of maximum possible temperature

questions.question: Which way does net heat transfer occur spontaneously between contacting objects?
choices: From lower to higher temperature without other effects
From higher to lower temperature
Only from greater to smaller mass
Only from solids into gases

questions.question: Why can a large warm object contain more thermal energy than a small hot object?
choices: Temperature alone fixes total energy
Large objects always have lower specific heat
Hot objects contain no stored internal energy
Total thermal energy depends on amount and substance as well as temperature

questions.question: Why does metal often feel colder than wood at the same room temperature?
choices: Metal usually transfers energy away from the hand faster
Metal must have a lower temperature
Wood produces heat without an energy source
Skin measures mass rather than energy transfer

questions.question: How does insulation reduce heat transfer?
choices: It limits one or more heat-transfer mechanisms
It creates cold energy
It guarantees no energy transfer ever occurs
It changes every material's chemical identity

questions.question: Why can warm air rise relative to cooler surrounding air?
choices: Warm air has no mass
Its atoms stop responding to gravity
Its lower density can produce buoyant motion
It always has a higher density

questions.question: Why does a high specific heat help water moderate temperature changes?
choices: Water cannot transfer thermal energy
A given energy transfer causes a smaller temperature change per unit mass
Water becomes solid whenever heated
Water creates energy whenever it cools

questions.question: Why can melting require energy without raising temperature during the phase change?
choices: Particles have no motion while melting
The supplied energy must be destroyed
The sample stops interacting with its surroundings
Energy changes particle arrangements and interactions

questions.question: Why can objects exchange thermal radiation across a vacuum?
choices: A vacuum is filled with circulating hot air
Electromagnetic waves require no material medium
Radiation occurs only by particle contact
Objects must first exchange matter

questions.question: A metal spoon warms in a hot drink. Which process transfers energy along the solid spoon?
choices: Conduction
Convection inside the solid
Evaporation
Condensation

questions.question: Water circulates in a heated pot as warmer water rises. Which process is illustrated?
choices: Radiation alone
Freezing
Convection
Diffusion of magnetic fields

questions.question: A 2 kg sample with specific heat 500 J/(kg·°C) warms by 3°C. Using Q = mcΔT, what energy is transferred?
Equal masses of two materials receive equal energy with no phase changes. The first has twice the specific heat. How does its temperature rise compare?
choices: It is half as large
It is twice as large
It is four times as large
It is the same

questions.question: A hot and a cool object contact each other in an insulated system, with no phase changes or other energy transfers. What is expected as they approach thermal equilibrium?
choices: Both increase temperature indefinitely
Both decrease temperature indefinitely
Only the more massive object changes temperature
The hot object cools while the cool object warms
